title: Suspicious program contacting an outside server
description: A workstation in the engineering department began making repeated outbound connections to an unfamiliar address shortly after a software download. The investigation aims to establish what ran, what it contacted, and whether data left the network.

sources.label: Engineering workstation WS-114
sources.description: Desktop used by one engineer. Isolated from the network on 2026-08-01.

sources.label: Perimeter traffic tap
sources.description: Mirror port at the office firewall.

sources.label: Internal DNS resolver
sources.description: Primary resolver for the office network.

evidence.title: Disk image of WS-114 system drive
evidence.description: Full forensic image of the system drive of workstation WS-114, taken after the workstation was isolated from the network.
evidence.text: Image acquired through a hardware write blocker. Partitions: EFI 260 MB, NTFS 465 GB. File system timeline begins 2026-07-29.
custody: Handed over for file system analysis

analyses.notes: File system timeline and recent file review.
findings: Unsigned installer found in a public download folder
A program named updater_setup.exe was created in the public downloads folder on 2026-08-01 shortly before the unusual network activity began. The file is not digitally signed.
medium
Executable copied to a second location
A copy of the same program exists under a user application data folder, which is consistent with an attempt to keep it after a reboot.
medium

evidence.title: Windows process creation events from WS-114
evidence.description: Process creation events exported from the workstation's security log covering the 24 hours around the first suspicious connection.
evidence.text:
2026-08-01 08:14:07 ProcessCreate Image=C:/Users/Public/Downloads/updater_setup.exe ParentImage=C:/Program Files/Browser/browser.exe User=CORP/e.rossi
2026-08-01 08:14:19 ProcessCreate Image=C:/Windows/System32/cmd.exe ParentImage=updater_setup.exe CommandLine="cmd.exe /c whoami && ipconfig /all"
2026-08-01 08:15:02 ProcessCreate Image=C:/Windows/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe ParentImage=updater_setup.exe CommandLine="powershell -nop -w hidden -enc [encoded text omitted]"

analyses.notes: Timeline of process events around the download.
findings: Downloaded program launched system commands within seconds

The downloaded program started a command window that listed the user name and network settings, then started a hidden PowerShell window. Reconnaissance followed by hidden scripting is a common pattern after a malicious download.
high
Hidden encoded PowerShell command executed
The PowerShell command used an encoded argument and a hidden window. The decoded content was not preserved in this export.
high

evidence.title: Packet capture of outbound traffic from WS-114
evidence.description: Summary of packets captured at the perimeter tap for the address of WS-114, covering 24 hours from the first suspicious connection.
evidence.text:
08:15:44 192.0.2.114:51822 -> 203.0.113.77:443 TLS ClientHello SNI=cdn-update-sync.example.net
08:16:44 192.0.2.114:51830 -> 203.0.113.77:443 TLS ClientHello SNI=cdn-update-sync.example.net
Summary: 412 connections in 24 h, interval 60 s +/- 2 s, same destination.

findings: Regular connections at one-minute intervals

The workstation contacted the same outside address almost exactly every 60 seconds for a full day. Such a fixed interval is typical of automated check-ins to a remote controller, not of human browsing.
high
Encrypted traffic to an unfamiliar update-themed domain
All connections used encrypted web traffic to a domain whose name suggests software updates but which is not used by any approved vendor.
medium

evidence.title: DNS query log for the update-themed domain
evidence.description: Resolver log lines for the domain contacted by WS-114, covering the first and later lookups.
evidence.text:
2026-08-01 08:15:41 client=192.0.2.114 query=cdn-update-sync.example.net type=A answer=203.0.113.77 ttl=60
2026-08-01 08:15:41 client=192.0.2.114 query=cdn-update-sync.example.net type=AAAA answer=NXDOMAIN
2026-08-01 08:16:41 client=192.0.2.114 query=cdn-update-sync.example.net type=A answer=203.0.113.77 ttl=60

findings: Very short lifetime on the domain record
The domain's address record expires after 60 seconds, which lets an operator move the destination quickly. Short lifetimes are common for infrastructure that is meant to be hard to block.
low

evidence.title: Memory dump of WS-114 in running state
evidence.description: Capture of the workstation's memory taken before it was powered off.
evidence.text: Process list at capture time includes updater_setup.exe (PID 5128) with an open TCP connection to 203.0.113.77:443 and powershell.exe (PID 6040) as its child process.

analyses.notes: Process tree and network connection listing.
findings: Suspicious program still running with a live connection
At capture time the downloaded program was still running and held an open connection to the outside address, which ties the program to the network traffic.
high

analyses.notes: Pattern scan of the memory dump in progress.
findings: Possible injected code region in PowerShell process
A memory region with execute permission and no backing file was found in the PowerShell process. This needs confirmation before it is treated as injected code.
medium

evidence.title: Registry autostart entries export from WS-114
evidence.description: Export of the per-user and machine autostart registry keys from WS-114.

findings: Program registered to start at every logon
An autostart entry named SyncHelper launches the downloaded program in the background each time the user logs in, so the program would survive a restart.
high

evidence.title: Browser download history for the workstation user
evidence.description: Download records from the user's web browser profile on WS-114.

findings: Program came from a forum link, not an approved source
The installer was downloaded about two minutes before it ran, from an unofficial site reached through a discussion forum thread.
medium

evidence.title: IT help desk ticket from the affected user
evidence.description: Ticket text submitted by the user describing the problem as they saw it.
evidence.text: User reports the PC felt slow after installing a tool that promised faster updates. A black command window flashed several times. User did not run any other new software.

evidence.title: Firewall alert screenshot for beacon-like connections
evidence.description: Screenshot of the firewall dashboard showing the alert raised for repeated connections to the outside address.
evidence.notes: Taken at the time the alert was reviewed.

findings: Screenshot timestamp matches the alert time
The image creation time matches the alert time shown on screen, so the screenshot appears to be a faithful capture of the dashboard.
info

evidence.title: Firewall log of allowed outbound connections
evidence.description: Firewall rows for connections from WS-114 to the outside address, with byte counts.

findings: Larger uploads during the night
Overnight connections sent about 50 KB each, far more than the roughly 600 bytes sent during the day. This suggests data was being sent out at night, but the content is not visible in these logs.
high
Outbound data exceeds data received
The workstation sent over forty times more data than it received on those connections, which is unusual for a normal software update.
medium

evidence.title: Authentication log for the affected user account
evidence.description: Logon and file-share access events for the user account during the night of 2026-08-01.
evidence.text:
2026-08-01 02:07:41 logon success user=CORP/e.rossi workstation=WS-114 type=network
2026-08-01 02:08:10 share access user=CORP/e.rossi path=//fs01/design/projects count=214
2026-08-01 02:09:55 share access user=CORP/e.rossi path=//fs01/design/archive count=96

findings: Many design files read in the middle of the night
The account read more than 300 design files from the file server between 02:08 and 02:10, outside normal working hours, shortly before the larger uploads to the outside address.
high
Activity not explained by the user's ticket
The help desk ticket describes only slowness. It does not mention being at the computer at 02:07, which raises the question of whether the activity was automated.
medium

evidence.title: Chat export between help desk and the user
evidence.description: Messages exchanged in the internal chat tool between the help desk agent and the user before the machine was isolated.
evidence.text:
[07:58] user: I installed it from a forum link, it said it speeds up updates.
[08:03] helpdesk: Please do not run it again. Can you tell me what the program is called?
[08:05] user: updater_setup, I think. It is still open in the corner.

links: The download recorded in the browser history is the program that appears as the first process in the creation log.
The hidden PowerShell session starts at 08:15:02 and the first outbound connection to the outside address is at 08:15:44.
The DNS lookups match the destination and timing of the captured connections.
The resolved address 203.0.113.77 is the same destination shown in the firewall log.
Packet capture and firewall log both show the same destination and connection volume.
The alert screenshot reports the same repeated connections found in the firewall log.
The alert described in the screenshot is consistent with the one-minute interval found in the packet capture.
The process held in memory is the same program that is registered to start at logon.
